items.title: China's backflipping robot maker Unitree pops in Shanghai debut
items.note: Unitree shares surged as much as 629% intraday on its STAR Market debut, becoming the first listed humanoid-robot maker in mainland China at close to a $66B valuation.

items.title: Meta trial that could reshape Facebook and Instagram gets underway
items.note: A bipartisan 29-state coalition opened a six-week federal trial in Oakland alleging Meta designed Instagram/Facebook to addict young users; Meta pegs potential penalties near $1.4T.

items.title: Etched's valuation doubles to $21B in a month
items.note: AI inference-chip startup raised $700M led by Jane Street (with Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia, a16z, Tiger Global and others), taking total funding to $1.9B.

items.title: Apple plugs image-processing hole ripe for spyware abuse
items.note: Apple patched CVE-2026-65346, a critical ImageIO integer-overflow bug (found by Meta's Red Team) that could enable zero-click code execution via a malicious image, across iOS/iPadOS/macOS.

items.title: OpenAI Is Slowing Down Its AI Training
items.note: Sam Altman told TIME 'it's a good time to slow down,' saying OpenAI is pausing frontier-model training after research showed signs of misalignment as capabilities advanced faster than expected.

items.title: OpenAI seeks to one-up Anthropic with new customer privacy protections
items.note: OpenAI is previewing 'Private Safety Processing' with early customers, a tool that flags cross-session misuse patterns (e.g. split-up cyberattack planning) while preserving zero data retention; broad launch planned for September.

items.title: China's LandSpace lands reusable rocket booster, closing the gap with SpaceX
items.note: LandSpace recovered the first stage of its Zhuque-3 rocket, becoming the third private company after SpaceX and Blue Origin to land an orbital-class booster.

items.title: Samsung raises advanced foundry prices by up to 15% as AI demand fills its 4nm lines
items.note: Samsung hiked SF4/SF5/8nm order prices 5-15% in July as TSMC's leading-edge capacity fills up on AI-chip demand; Chinese customers reportedly accepted the steepest increases.

items.title: First Nvidia H200 shipments reach China as ByteDance and Tencent take deliveries
items.note: ByteDance and Tencent reportedly each received about 10,000 Nvidia H200 chips as Beijing eases its import block, though most licensed units must stay in Hong Kong for now.

items.title: CISA gives feds 3 days to fix actively exploited Ray RCE bug
items.note: CISA added a code-injection flaw in Ray, the open-source distributed-computing framework used by Amazon, Apple and OpenAI for ML workloads, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

items.title: Z.ai launches GLM-5.3 with claimed 50% gain on coding benchmark
items.note: Zhipu's international brand shipped GLM-5.3, targeting coding agents, tool use and defensive cybersecurity work; open-weights release promised two weeks later.

items.title: Pony.ai's overseas robotaxi pipeline tops 4,000 vehicles
items.note: Pipeline includes a 2,000+ vehicle Uber deployment deal in Europe plus services in Luxembourg, Singapore and Croatia; Q2 robotaxi revenue surged 691% year over year.

items.title: Stock Market Today (Aug. 19, 2026): S&P 500 rises despite tech weakness as health care, cyclicals jump
items.note: Chip and tech stocks lagged the broader market amid rising bond yields, days ahead of Nvidia's August 26 earnings report.

items.title: ByteDance and Hollywood reach agreement over AI video IP rights
items.note: The Motion Picture Association's first-ever AI-company deal adds copyright guardrails to ByteDance's Seedance video and Seedream image-generation models, months after an MPA cease-and-desist letter.

items.title: Baidu Q2 2026 earnings miss as ad revenue falls 19%
items.note: Net profit plunged 68% year over year to roughly $341.6M even as AI cloud infrastructure revenue grew 50%; fifth straight quarter of revenue decline.

items.title: Xiaomi's profit drops again as the memory crunch squeezes its phones
items.note: Adjusted net profit fell roughly 43% as soaring memory-chip costs from the global AI-driven shortage hit smartphone margins; third straight quarterly profit decline.

items.title: Perplexity's free AI offer left it with millions more users in India
items.note: Giving free premium access to Airtel's 360M customers pushed Perplexity's India in-app revenue well above its 2026 average, per the company's growth data.
